title: Which of these four pairs of numbers are co-prime?
description: Four pairs of numbers are each split into rows of primes and the rows are compared. A pair is co-prime when no prime is common to both rows.
teaching_notes: One idea: a pair of numbers is co-prime when their rows of primes share no prime. Watch for students who guess from the size or look of the numbers and never compare the primes.

video_script.why: The child decides whether each pair is co-prime by writing the rows of primes and looking for a common prime, the way the book does for forty and two hundred and thirty one.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four pairs: thirty and forty five, fifty seven and eighty five, one hundred and twenty one and one thousand three hundred and thirty one, three hundred and forty three and two hundred and sixteen
video_script.anchor: four pairs of numbers, each with two rows of primes and the common primes ringed
video_script.payoff_line: A pair is co-prime only when no prime is common to both rows

final_answer.value: a. No; b. Yes; c. No; d. Yes
final_answer.spoken: not co-prime, co-prime, not co-prime, co-prime

hold_back: a. No; b. Yes; c. No; d. Yes
maths_rules: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5 and 45 = 3 × 3 × 5: common primes 3 and 5, so not co-prime
57 = 3 × 19 and 85 = 5 × 17: no common prime, so co-prime
121 = 11 × 11 and 1331 = 11 × 11 × 11: common prime 11, so not co-prime
343 = 7 × 7 × 7 and 216 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3: no common prime, so co-prime
video_script.design: Each pair gets two rows of primes. The common primes, if any, are ringed.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about four pairs of numbers.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first pair is thirty and forty five. The second is fifty seven and eighty five.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The third is one hundred and twenty one and one thousand three hundred and thirty one.
<bookmark mark='fourth'/>The fourth is three hundred and forty three and two hundred and sixteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Guess first. Which of the pairs are co-prime?

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book. We write the row of primes of each number.
<bookmark mark='ring'/>Two numbers are co-prime when no prime is common to both rows.

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Step one, take thirty and forty five. Thirty is two times three times five, and forty five is three times three times five.
<bookmark mark='common'/>The primes three and five are common, so they are not co-prime.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 57 = 3 × 19 and 85 = 5 × 17; no prime is common, so they are co-prime

marks.none: the two rows are compared and no prime matches

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Step two, take fifty seven and eighty five. Fifty seven is three times nineteen, and eighty five is five times seventeen.
<bookmark mark='none'/>No prime is common, so they are co-prime.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 121 = 11 × 11 and 1331 = 11 × 11 × 11; the prime 11 is common, so they are not co-prime

marks.common: the 11s are ringed in both rows

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Step three, take one hundred and twenty one and one thousand three hundred and thirty one. The first is eleven times eleven.
<bookmark mark='common'/>The second is eleven times eleven times eleven. The prime eleven is common, so they are not co-prime.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 343 = 7 × 7 × 7 and 216 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3; no prime is common, so they are co-prime

marks.none: the two rows are compared and no prime matches

beats.colours: 7s in rose, 2s in teal, 3s in amber
narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Step four, take three hundred and forty three and two hundred and sixteen. The first is seven times seven times seven.
<bookmark mark='none'/>The second has three twos and three threes. No prime is common, so they are co-prime.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check the common primes: 15 divides 30 and 45 (30 ÷ 15 = 2, 45 ÷ 15 = 3); 11 divides 121 and 1331 (121 ÷ 11 = 11, 1331 ÷ 11 = 121)
narration: <bookmark mark='fifteen'/>Step five, check the common primes. Three times five is fifteen, and fifteen divides thirty and forty five exactly.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Eleven divides one hundred and twenty one and one thousand three hundred and thirty one exactly.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a. No; b. Yes; c. No; d. Yes

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The first and third pairs are not co-prime. The second and fourth pairs are co-prime.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>A pair is co-prime only when no prime is common to both rows.
